title: NIDCD says a hearing problem can affect speech and language
summary: NIDCD says a hearing problem can affect speech and language, and that a hearing test is often part of a speech and language evaluation.
body: The NIDCD milestone page says that sometimes a delay may be caused by hearing loss, and sometimes by a speech or language disorder. It also says a hearing test is often included when a speech-language pathologist evaluates a child, because a hearing problem can affect speech and language development. The page tells a worried caregiver to talk with the child's doctor. It does not describe one child, and it does not give steps for a hearing screening. This is the institute's general statement.

sources.title: Speech and Language Developmental Milestones
sources.author: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. The page prints NIH Publication No. 00-4781, September 2010, and no later review date. Supports the sentences that a delay may be caused by hearing loss and that a hearing problem can affect speech and language development.
